s2.p2: It allows you to describe several strategies of the object's behavior with the ability to choose the desired strategy.
s2.p3: First, let's create a few helper modules, which you can then import into the main module of the class.
s2.p20: An instance of this class will sort the resulting array of objects according to the specified strategy.
s2.p21: In this example, the instance can use three collation strategies:
s2.p22:
| **key** | Sort by a given key.
^^Each element (object) of the array must have a property with an appropriate name.^^ |
s2.p23:
| **sum-of-all-numeric-fields** | Sort by the sum of all numeric properties of the object.
^^All numeric properties of the object that is an element of the original (sorted) array will be summed.
The source array will be sorted by the sum of the numeric properties of the objects.^^ |
s2.p24:
| **array-field-length** | Sort by length of the array property.
^^All objects that are elements of the original (sortable) array must have an array property.
The source array will be sorted by the length of the property array.^^ |
s2.p25: Switching from one strategy to another occurs by changing the **valueOf** property of each element of the source array.
s2.p28: Now let's deal with the initial data. We will use three arrays of objects with a different set of properties.
